title: Can two new values leave the mean unchanged?
description: The data five, five, ten and twenty four has mean eleven, and two new values are added, one four below eleven and one four above. The board finds the new sum and the new mean. Keeko's doubt is that the mean must change whenever new values come in.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shortfall below the mean and an equal surplus above it cancel, so the mean stays where it was. Watch for students who think any new value must move the mean.

source: The data 5, 5, 10, 24 has mean 11. Include 2 values, one 4 b
video_script.why: The child sees that new values placed evenly on both sides of the mean leave the mean where it is.
video_script.substitution: Place one new value below the mean and one above it by the same gap, then compare the new sum and the new count.
video_script.anchor: a number line with dots at five, five, ten and twenty four, the mean marker at eleven, and two new dots waiting at seven and fifteen
video_script.wrong_answer: the mean must change when two new values come in
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the mean always changes when new values are included. Here one new value is four below the mean and one is four above, so the shortfall and the surplus cancel and the mean stays.
never_show: the final answer line before the answer beat
maths_rules: old sum = 44, old count 4, old mean 11
shortfall of 7 below 11 is 4; surplus of 15 above 11 is 4; 4 and 4 cancel
balance check: old left distances 6 + 6 + 1 = 13, old right 13; new left 13 + 4 = 17, new right 13 + 4 = 17
video_script.design: One idea: a shortfall and an equal surplus cancel, so the mean stays. The dots and the mean marker stay from ground to the end of the idea part. Wrong idea: the mean must change when values come in.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the same data, with mean eleven.
<bookmark mark='dots'/>The data is five, five, ten and twenty four, and the mean marker sits at eleven.
<bookmark mark='new'/>Two new values join, one four below eleven and one four above. Will the mean change?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board while the line stays in view

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.short: a bracket from the marker down to the dot at 7 appears with the label shortfall

narration: <bookmark mark='short'/>A value below the mean falls short of it by some gap on the line. That gap is called the shortfall.
<bookmark mark='surplus'/>A value above the mean goes past it by some gap on the line. That gap is called the surplus.

beats.on_screen: Given: data 5, 5, 10, 24 with mean 11; new values 4 below 11 and 4 above 11

marks.given: the data, its mean and the two new values are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the data five, five, ten and twenty four with mean eleven, and two new values.

beats.on_screen: To find: the new mean, and whether it is unchanged

marks.find: the thing to find is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the new mean, and see whether it is unchanged.

marks.low: 11 − 4 = 7 is written and a dot lands at 7
marks.high: 11 + 4 = 15 is written and a dot lands at 15

narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Step one, the new values. The value that is four below eleven is seven.
<bookmark mark='high'/>The value that is four above eleven is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, the new sum. The old sum is forty four, and forty four plus seven plus fifteen is sixty six.
<bookmark mark='count'/>There are now six values in the data, not four.

marks.divide: 66 ÷ 6 = 11 is written and the marker stays at 11

narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>Step three, the new mean. Sixty six divided by six is eleven.

beats.on_screen: shortfall 4 and surplus 4 cancel, so the mean stays 11

marks.cancel: the blue 4 and the orange 4 are linked and crossed out together

narration: <bookmark mark='cancel'/>Step four, compare. The shortfall of four and the surplus of four cancel each other.

marks.ans: the answer line is boxed and the marker rests at 11

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The mean stays eleven.
An equal shortfall and surplus leave the mean where it was.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble says the mean must change when new values come in
marks.fix: the distances show left 13 plus 4 and right 13 plus 4, both 17
marks.rule: the bubble is struck through and the balance at 11 is circled

beats.colours: warning colour for the struck bubble
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the mean must change when two new values come in.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The old distances were thirteen on each side. The new dots add four to each side, so both sides make seventeen.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The balance is kept, so the mean does not move.
